 Taiwan Semiconductor Slipped 14% This Month Amidst Tech Contraction: 175% Gains to Materialize According to One Wall Street Desk
 By Alex Sirois

 Quick Read
 TSM (NYSE:TSM) tumbled 14% in a month despite a Q3 earnings beat, while analysts keep raising estimates and see 62% upside.
 Intel plunged 41% and United Microelectronics fell 30%, so the whole foundry group sold off harder than TSM.
 CEO C.C. Wei says "demand is higher than supply," the core of the bull case that leans toward opportunity.

 Taiwan Semiconductor ( NYSE:TSM | TSM Price Prediction ) currently trades at $362.55, while Wall Street’s average price target stands at $586.69. That leaves an implied gap of 61.8% between the share price and where analysts think the stock belongs.
 Taiwan Semiconductor is the world’s largest dedicated foundry and the main supplier of leading-edge chips to AI and high-performance computing (HPC) customers. HPC made up 68% [ 1 ] of third-quarter revenue, and management expects full-year revenue growth of around 44% in U.S. dollar terms.

 One analyst goes much further. Aletheia Capital holds a Street-high target of $1,000.00, which implies about 175.8% upside. With even the consensus gap above 40%, the key question is whether the market is mispricing a growth story or correctly pricing in a cyclical peak.
 Chip Stocks Sold Off Hard, and TSM Lost a Month of Gains in a Week
 TSM fell 13.72% over the past month, and 12.29% of that came in the past week alone. The S&P 500 slipped 4.73% over the same month. The selling hit the whole sector. Questions about AI revenue pulled semiconductor stocks off their October highs, a broad chip-stock selloff followed, and Washington moved to tighten AI chip rules (per recent industry wire coverage) [ 2 ] .
 Taiwan Semiconductor’s own results held up. Third-quarter EPS of $4.60 [ 3 ] beat the $4.46 consensus, and October revenue rose 59.7% [ 4 ] year over year. Gross margin fell 1.3 percentage points [ 3 ] sequentially to 66.4% as 2nm production scaled up, management warned overseas fab dilution could expand to 3%-4% [ 1 ] , and the 2026 capital budget stands at $60 billion to $64 billion.
 Analysts Keep Raising Estimates While the Stock Falls
 The ratings are close to unanimous:
 Strong Buy: 6
 Buy: 14
 Hold: 1
 Sell: 0
 The core bull thesis is a supply shortage. Chief executive C.C. Wei said “demand is higher than supply, and we are working very hard to narrow the gap.” [ 1 ] Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion implies 58% year-over-year growth at the midpoint.
 Estimates are rising even as the stock falls. The average 2027 EPS estimate stands at $23.3853, up from $21.9189 a month ago, with 10 upward revisions in the past seven days and none lower. That leaves the stock at about 18x forward earnings.
 N2 capacity is expected to more than double in 2027 [ 1 ] , A14 volume production is scheduled for 2028, and Arizona’s second fab is targeting volume output in the third quarter of 2027. Aletheia’s model assumes both higher earnings and a richer multiple, driven by foundry pricing power . The next-highest targets cluster at $670.00 (DA Davidson) and $600.00 (Barclays and UBS). Targets are opinions, though, and the $1,000 call is an outlier.
 Most Foundry Peers Fell Even Harder
 The whole foundry group sold off together, and TSM held up better than most.
 Intel ( NASDAQ:INTC ) dropped 40.6% over the month to $54.67. Against a $90.65 target, that implies 65.8% upside, but 36 analysts rate it Hold versus 12 bullish calls. That is slightly more upside than TSM, with far less conviction behind it.
 United Microelectronics ( NYSE:UMC ) fell 30.43% to $13.97. Its $17.20 target implies just 23.1% upside, and analyst coverage is thin (one Buy and three Strong Sell ratings).
 GlobalFoundries ( NASDAQ:GFS ) slid 13.62% to $39.83. Its $64.77 target implies 62.6% upside, close to TSM’s, though 9 of its analysts sit at Hold.
 Intel carries the highest implied upside among these stocks, but analysts are mostly lukewarm on it. TSM offers nearly as much upside with almost no dissent among analysts.
 Still Beating the S&P 500 Despite the Drop
 At $362.55, TSM sits well below its 52-week high of $487.47. The 21 analysts covering it put the average target at $586.69, which implies 61.8% upside.
 Even after the selloff, TSM is up 20.22% year to date. The S&P 500 is up 7.09% over the same stretch. Over the past month, TSM fell 13.72% while the index fell 4.73%. The stock trades at about 24 times trailing earnings.
 Supply Shortage Tips This Toward Opportunity
 Taiwan Semiconductor’s outlook improves if AI customers keep spending at their current pace and the 2nm ramp delivers the volume growth management expects through 2027. Earnings estimates would keep rising, the forward multiple would compress on its own, and the $586.69 consensus becomes reachable without extreme assumptions.
 Sellers take control if AI revenue concerns turn into actual order cuts. Heavy spending, overseas fab dilution and weaker consumer segments would then pressure margins just as growth slows. Tighter Washington chip rules add a risk that analyst models struggle to price.
 I lean toward opportunity. Earnings estimates are rising while the stock falls, and the selloff has hit the whole sector. The $1,000 target requires multiple expansion on top of earnings growth. The consensus target only needs the current trend to hold.
